name: JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-Domain Field (Hubble)
blurb: The JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-Domain Field, a deep survey field, seen by Hubble.
label: jwstneptdf01wfc-hubble
story: A clean window near the North Ecliptic Pole, chosen for its faint foreground glow and lack of bright sources in front of the distant galaxies. Webb can watch it at any time of year, and Hubble's survey here turned up transients, most expected to be supernovae, and variable sources that are mostly active galaxies.

claims.text: The JWST NEP Time-Domain Field lies near the North Ecliptic Pole in JWST's northern Continuous Viewing Zone
The field has the lowest possible zodiacal foreground and no bright sources
JWST can observe the field at any time of year
Hubble's TREASUREHUNT imaging found transients, mostly supernovae, and variable candidates, mostly AGN
JWST-NEP-TDF-01WFC is a target of Hubble program 16252, TREASUREHUNT
